The visit includes a proposed trade deal discussion and a reception for the US independence anniversary. Rubio previously stated the US is close to finalizing the trade pact.
items.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio Arrives in Mumbai for Trade and Energy Talks

items.summary: India's merchandise exports to the United Kingdom rose 8% to $2.43 billion in August and September 2026, while imports from Britain fell 16.8% to $1.36 billion, following the July 15 operationalization of the CETA free trade agreement. Experts note that full potential realization is pending as traders adjust to the new framework.
items.title: India-UK Trade Deal Boosts Exports, Cuts Imports in Early Months

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Mumbai for a three-day visit to India, focusing on trade, energy, and defense. He is set to meet with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar to discuss advancing bilateral ties and a proposed trade pact. The visit also addresses critical technologies and the West Asia crisis, occurring amidst ongoing friction in India-US relations.
items.title: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio Arrives in India for Trade and Energy Talks

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated during his visit to Mumbai that an India-US trade deal is expected to be finalized shortly. Rubio expressed optimism regarding an announcement in the near future, noting that only a few issues remain to be resolved. During the visit, Rubio also highlighted India's substantial progress in diversifying its energy sources and discussed potential cooperation in refining Venezuelan crude with Reliance Industries. The meeting between Rubio and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar focused on strengthening bilateral ties in defence, security, technology, and critical minerals.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio Announces Imminent India-US Trade Deal

items.summary: K Annamalai, chief of the We The Leaders Foundation, expressed happiness regarding RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's recent comments on religious inclusivity in India. Annamalai welcomed Bhagwat's statement affirming that Muslims and other religious communities have a place in the country. The remarks were made by Bhagwat during his visit to the United States. Aryan Singh of The Times of India reported on the exchange.
items.title: Annamalai Welcomes Bhagwat's Remarks on Religious Inclusivity in India

items.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut faced criticism for suggesting India learn from Albania's violent student protests, which targeted democratic institutions. Former colleague Priyanka Chaturvedi condemned the remarks, warning against destabilizing institutions and noting Albania's history under dictatorship. The BJP also slammed Raut, while context reveals 388 people were charged in Albania amid corruption allegations and public anger.
items.title: Shiv Sena Leader Criticized for Suggesting India Learn from Albania Protests

items.summary: The 17th UN biodiversity conference opened in Yerevan, Armenia, on Monday. Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the Convention on Biological Diversity, stated that while progress has been made on the Kunming-Montreal framework, action remains insufficient. She called for strengthened alignment and broader participation. Armenian Environment Minister Hambardzum Matevosyan was elected president for a two-year term. The event, themed 'Taking Action for Nature,' runs through October 30, 2026.
items.title: UN Biodiversity Conference Opens in Armenia with New President

items.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Bulgarian Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova held talks in Beijing, agreeing to strengthen their strategic partnership. Wang Yi emphasized China's readiness to support Bulgaria's development and the Belt and Road initiative, while Petrova affirmed Bulgaria's commitment to the one-China principle. Both sides expressed a desire to deepen cooperation in trade, culture, and high-tech sectors, and to enhance connectivity between East and West.
items.title: Chinese and Bulgarian Foreign Ministers Discuss Strategic Partnership and Regional Cooperation

items.summary: The PyTorch team at Hugging Face released version 2.15, focusing on improving the MPS backend for Macs. Key updates include FP8 support, which halves memory usage for tensors, and significant speedups for large language models. Mixture-of-experts models now decode 5–6.5× faster, while dense models benefit from optimized linear layers. The release also addresses memory issues in video generation, reducing peak driver memory from 270 GiB to 8 GiB for Wan2.2. Additionally, image editing workflows are fixed, and new operations like complex LU factorization now run directly on the GPU. Users require macOS 15 or later and Python 3.11 or later.
items.title: PyTorch 2.15 Brings Faster LLM Decoding and FP8 Support to Mac

items.summary: Official data indicates China's GDP grew 4.6% year on year in the first three quarters. CGTN anchor Michael Wang explains that production and consumption reinforce each other, noting that stronger industrial capacity makes goods more affordable and boosts household purchasing power. This dynamic suggests the growth is supported by both supply-side capacity and demand-side purchasing power.
items.title: China's GDP Growth Driven by Mutual Reinforcement of Output and Demand

items.summary: Tim Adams, president and CEO of the Institute of International Finance (IIF), stated that China's capital markets are deepening and becoming increasingly international. Speaking to CGTN's Yu Bokun in Beijing, Adams noted that as China's role in global trade and financing grows, these markets are attracting growing interest from investors worldwide.
items.title: IIF CEO Says China's Capital Markets Attract Growing Global Investor Interest

items.summary: The Philippines is advancing plans to introduce nuclear power into its electricity mix to strengthen energy security and support clean energy goals. Energy Secretary Sharon Garin cited rising electricity demand, reliance on imported fuels, and regional security concerns as drivers. The government targets 1.2 GW of nuclear capacity by 2032, potentially increasing to 4.8 GW by 2050, alongside renewable energy targets. While private sector players like Meralco and Aboitiz Power are exploring options, officials caution that nuclear will not automatically reduce electricity prices and emphasize the need for robust regulatory frameworks and international cooperation.
items.title: Philippines Advances Nuclear Power Plans Amid Rising Energy Demand

items.summary: India has updated its Nationally Determined Contribution to target 60% non-fossil power capacity by 2035. While the country met its 2030 target of 50% five years early, current power systems face strain with daytime demand over 267 GW and a shortfall exceeding 7.7 GW after sunset. The commentary notes that achieving the 2035 goal depends on navigating uncertainties in economic growth, demand-side interventions, and supply-side constraints like solar panel costs. Factors such as global conflicts, trade disputes, and geopolitical shocks could significantly alter the transition trajectory, making the target a calibrated response to a volatile environment rather than a fixed commitment.
items.title: India's Climate Targets Face Geopolitical and Economic Uncertainty

items.summary: Spanish renewable energy company Acciona Energía has opened two wind farms in Croatia with a combined capacity of 72 MW. The Opor and Boraja II projects began supplying electricity to the national grid and are linked to 12-year contracts for difference. The developments created up to 400 direct jobs and are expected to generate around 203 GWh of clean electricity annually.
items.title: Acciona Energía Opens Two Wind Farms in Croatia

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, expressed emotional solidarity with co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who remain in judicial custody over a Jantar Mantar trespassing case. Dipke urged the public to remember the leaders during the festive season, stating that true strength lies in sacrifice and that their conduct reflects a commitment to non-violence. Authorities extended their custody following allegations of breaching bonds at a de-notified protest site.
items.title: Abhijeet Dipke Expresses Solidarity With CJP Leaders In Custody

items.summary: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated that targeted curfews contributed to overnight calm in Paris. Meanwhile, Italy deployed troops to Milan, and Zelenskyy met Nordic leaders in Oslo. France also announced economic aid and court actions against rioters.
items.title: French PM cites curfews for calm amid European unrest and diplomatic talks

items.summary: French cloud provider OVHcloud warned users that attackers compromised its open-source CLI tool to steal secrets. CEO Octave Klaba stated versions 0.11.0 through 0.15.0 were infected, while 0.10.0 and 0.16.0 remained clean. The incident, detected on October 19, 2026, involved a hijacked GitHub account. Researchers linked the attack to the GlassWorm group, noting affected platforms include macOS, Linux, and Windows. Users are urged to revoke all secrets.
items.title: OVHcloud CLI Compromised with Malware Stealing Developer Secrets

items.summary: Manipur Chief Minister Y Khemchand Singh met with INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress chief Okram Ibobi Singh, to review security following the killing of three firewood collectors in Kangpokpi. Opposition leaders cited a complete failure of law and order. The CM assured that the matter would be investigated. Ibobi Singh stated that law and order has completely failed in the state.
items.title: Manipur CM Meets INDIA Bloc Leaders After Three Civilians Killed in Kangpokpi

items.summary: US special envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Norway for talks with Volodymyr Zelensky as relations between Kyiv and the US President Donald Trump deteriorate. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre aims to steer relations toward a constructive path. Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied accusations of withholding intelligence, though Ukrainian adviser Serhii Beskrestnov claimed a lack of warnings cost lives. Discussions include Starlink and missile interceptors.
items.title: Zelensky Prepares for Oslo Talks Amid US-Ukraine Tensions

items.summary: BloombergNEF states that $332 billion in new copper mine investment is required to prevent a global supply deficit by 2050. Without this funding, shortages could hinder electrification efforts. The report highlights that demand is projected to rise significantly while supply remains constrained, potentially forcing manufacturers to seek alternatives and slowing the deployment of electric vehicles and grids.
items.title: BloombergNEF Warns of Copper Deficit Unless $332 Billion Invested

items.summary: A 43-year-old man faces charges after hitting Australian MP Helen Haines with a car in Victoria. Haines, 65, remains in critical condition following surgery and the loss of one leg. Police allege the incident was targeted. The suspect's father and partner stated they had known Haines for over 20 years. Local activist Ricky Jefferies intervened, removing a knife from the suspect. The community has held vigils as Haines recovers.
items.title: Man Charged After Attacking Australian MP in Victoria

items.summary: Lisbon police arrested 55 people and cleared a tent camp in Rossio Square, citing illegal gatherings. Protesters resisted, throwing objects at officers before being expelled. While 55 arrests and 228 seized structures were confirmed by police, protesters claimed about 30 were injured. The movement vows to continue, with plans for a new protest in Lisbon and potential occupation of the Prime Minister's home.
items.title: Lisbon Police Arrest 55 Housing Protesters and Clear Rossio Camp

items.summary: Sheffield City Council increased crisis payments for households facing severe financial difficulties by £30. Single-person households now receive £95, two-person households £110, and larger families up to £130. The change follows a review finding 50,000 households struggling to pay bills. Councillor Elle Dodd stated the move aims to provide immediate support and tackle poverty root causes.
items.title: Sheffield Council Raises Crisis Payments for Struggling Households

items.summary: Ahold Delhaize confirmed a recent cyberattack disrupted its websites, apps, and customer service platforms across Europe and the United States, though physical stores remained open. The company reported restoring some systems while others remain offline. CEO Frans Muller apologized for the inconvenience and stated that an ongoing investigation has not found evidence of stolen customer or associate data. This marks the second major attack on the retailer in recent years.
items.title: Ahold Delhaize Confirms Cyberattack Disrupted Services Across US and Europe

items.summary: Four individuals died on October 15 while fighting a wildfire in Indonesia's Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park. The victims included a national park staff member, two employees of a hotel security company, and a state firefighter. A fifth person, a volunteer, was evacuated with burn injuries. The fire, fueled by El Niño and Indian Ocean Dipole patterns, was declared under control on October 14 but reignited the next morning. Officials noted the severity of the current fires compared to previous crises. The incident has prompted calls to strengthen early warning systems and emergency response readiness.
items.title: Wildfire in Mount Bromo National Park Kills Four Firefighters

items.summary: A research team led by the University of Science and Technology of China developed a framework to assess fire risks in building-integrated photovoltaic façades. Using data-driven analysis and expert judgment, they identified electrical conditions and material properties as dominant risk factors. The framework proposes 15 safety measures, prioritizing rapid shutdown and ignition prevention to enhance fire resilience and limit fire spread.
items.title: New Framework Prioritizes Fire Protection for BIPV Façades

items.summary: French security forces arrested a man believed to be connected to ultra-left movements regarding the burning of a historic town hall in Limoges. Anti-terror police and the Counter-Terrorism Sub-Directorate are investigating the suspected arson. Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin stated that if prosecutors take up the case, it implies a terrorist act organized by individuals from the far left. The incident has become a symbol of recent violent rioting.
items.title: France Arrests Man Linked to Limoges Town Hall Fire

items.summary: President Trump is pursuing Russia-friendly actions to conclude the war in Ukraine. This approach coincides with rising energy costs ahead of the U.S. midterms. The article notes his fluctuating relationship with Russia is resurfacing as he seeks a resolution.
items.title: Trump Seeks Ukraine War End With Russia-Friendly Moves Amid Energy Concerns

items.summary: Yelp is introducing a new feature called Check for Me, allowing users to employ a voice agent to call restaurants and check wait times. This addition complements Yelp's existing voice solutions for businesses. The platform is also updating its AI assistant with better personalization, chat history access, and new list-building capabilities. Additionally, Yelp is launching a paid product, Smart Lead Reply, for business owners to manage customer inquiries.
items.title: Yelp Adds Voice Agent Feature to Check Restaurant Wait Times

items.summary: Otter.ai announced a $320 million investment from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund to fuel enterprise growth and product innovation. The startup, which recently crossed $100 million in annual recurring revenue, plans to use the capital for international expansion and go-to-market strategy. While the company reported 40 million users, it declined to provide figures on monthly active users or churn.
items.title: Otter.ai Secures $320 Million Growth Funding from General Catalyst

items.summary: CNET Group launched TechPulse, a free iOS and Android app that aggregates content from ZDNET, CNET, PCMag, Mashable, Lifehacker, and ExtremeTech. The EIC of the group described the tool as an algorithm-free alternative to tedious homepage visits, allowing users to select specific publications. The app integrates articles, videos, and expert reviews without requiring a subscription.
items.title: CNET Group Launches Free Tech News Aggregator App

items.summary: The World Health Organization reports that Bangladesh is facing the world's most severe measles outbreak, driven by weak data and vaccination gaps. Since mid-March, the country has recorded 202,000 suspected cases, including 22,000 confirmed ones, surpassing any other nation this year. The crisis has resulted in 1,147 deaths, with 94% occurring among children under five, prompting experts to warn other nations about the risks of falling immunization rates.
items.title: Bangladesh Battles World's Worst Measles Outbreak Amid Vaccination Gaps

items.summary: Norwegian and Danish funds invested in a 49% equity stake of the 500 MW Ixus Bugallon solar project in the Philippines. Vena Energy holds the remaining 51%. The project reached financial close in July 2026 after securing $310 million in senior loans. Norway's Minister of International Development, Åsmund Aukrust, stated the investment exemplifies mobilizing private capital for renewable energy.
items.title: Norwegian and Danish funds invest in Philippine solar project

items.summary: An instructor at Force Academy in Chongqing describes a pedagogical strategy where a student project is handed to a second student for verification. This process reveals gaps in reproducibility and measurement design that the original author may have overlooked. The instructor notes that while Generative AI lowers the cost of producing convincing work, it does not guarantee understanding. Consequently, the handoff serves as a stronger test of a student's grasp of their project than the initial successful run alone, forcing a redesign of studies to ensure clarity and robustness.
items.title: A Teacher Tests Student Work Through a Second-User Handoff

items.summary: Kim Leadbeater, sister of murdered MP Jo Cox, called on Australia to treat the serious injury of MP Helen Haines as a catalyst for calmer political discourse. Leadbeater stated that horrific attacks do not occur in a vacuum but are part of a wider culture. She expressed frustration that the need to address toxic political environments remains a recurring conversation. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and other politicians echoed these calls for unity and civilised debate. Leadbeater highlighted the industrial scale of online abuse she and others face, noting that while shock fades, the impact on victims and their families is lasting.
items.title: Sister of murdered UK MP Jo Cox wants Australia to tone down rhetoric
